docs.title: rn-forge-django
docs.text:
rn-forge-django is the opinionated Django/DRF integration layer built on top of rn-forge-commons.

It provides:

  • abstract model base classes: status/audit fields, natural-key fixture support, opt-in validation-on-save
  • a typed, auto-reloading settings facade for the RN_FORGE_DJANGO Django setting
  • an installable auth app: the /auth routes over rn-forge-auth, sessions, and DRF authentication and permission classes
  • DRF base views and mixins: tabular export/import and batch create/delete (transfer extra), audit-field population, auth-aware permissions
  • Excel-to-fixture generation for Django loaddata

Use the guides for common workflows and the API reference for module details.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: Notable changes to rn-forge-django, newest first, in the Keep a Changelog format.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• The /auth surface over rn-forge-auth, in rn_forge.django.auth. auth_urlpatterns(config, prefix="auth"), configured by AuthRoutesConfig, serves providers, login/{provider}, callback/{provider}, session, logout, logout/all, backchannel-logout/{provider} and login/password over LoginFlow. Providers, the account resolver and the authorization context provider are rn-forge-auth objects passed in the configuration; there is no settings block for them. The development provider exists only under DEBUG. A callback error redirects to the error route with one of access_denied, account_not_provisioned and login_failed.
  • Login transactions, replay records and revoked session IDs in Django's cache: CacheTransactionStore and CacheReplayStore, behind the __Host-login-tx cookie. The redis extra names rn-forge-auth[redis], the client for Django's Redis cache backend.
  • Sessions on django.contrib.sessions (db or cached_db). SESSION_SETTINGS carries the __Host-session cookie settings. Sessions applies a 30-minute sliding idle timeout and a 12-hour absolute timeout (AuthRoutesConfig.idle_timeout and absolute_timeout), and deletes a session whose version differs from its account's, whose account is inactive, or whose session_ref is revoked. GET /auth/session does not extend the session. rotate_session gives a session a new ID after a privilege change.
  • CSRF protection for session routes. AuthCsrfMiddleware adds the Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site rejection and the Bearer Authorization exemption to CsrfViewMiddleware. CSRF_SETTINGS configures Angular's XSRF-TOKEN cookie and X-XSRF-TOKEN header, and csrf_failure_view answers the 403 csrf-failed problem. /auth/session always sets the cookie, and login and logout rotate the token. enforce_csrf runs the same check for DRF views, which are csrf_exempt.
  • RN_FORGE_DJANGO["AUTH"]["PROBLEM_TYPE_BASE"]. auth_urlpatterns raises ImproperlyConfigured without it, so csrf-failed and forbidden differ in type, and refuses unsafe session, CSRF and cache settings at startup.
  • Rate limiting: FixedWindowLimiter and RateLimit, a fixed-window counter over Django's cache. /auth/login/password is limited per client and per username, callbacks per client, with limits on AuthRoutesConfig. A limited request is a 429 too-many-requests problem with Retry-After.
  • Audit events on the rn_forge.audit.auth AppLogger channel: login success and failure, logout, account provisioned, rejected and disabled, authorization denied and rate limiting.
  • Account resolution. DjangoAccountResolver is an AccountResolver over the Django user model and the ExternalAccount link model, unique on (issuer, subject), with the auth app's first migration, which also adds AccountState for the session version. A per-provider ProviderPolicy sets existing or jit provisioning, an email-domain allowlist and the domains for which a verified email links to an existing user; an optional sync hook copies attributes at each login, and link records service accounts. DjangoAccountStateWriter persists session versions and the active flag.
  • Authorization from Django groups and permissions: DjangoAuthorizationContextProvider (staff and superuser bypass as roles), connect_authorization_signals for cache invalidation, PermissionKeyPermission and ResourcePolicyViewMixin.
  • PrincipalSessionAuthentication yields a session principal from Sessions.read and enforces CSRF; sessions_for(config) builds its Sessions from AuthRoutesConfig. A request with an Authorization header is authenticated by the bearer class alone.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• rn_forge_django_settings is built on first use, so a settings module can import this package before it defines RN_FORGE_DJANGO.
  • problem_details_exception_handler renders with PROBLEM_TYPE_BASE when it is set.
  • Breaking: PrincipalBearerAuthentication and JWKSBearerAuthentication need accounts and contexts class attributes. They resolve the token's (issuer, subject) through AccountResolver.lookup (never provisioning) and answer 401 for an unlinked or inactive account. The principal's subject is the account ID, its roles, tenant and attributes come from the authorization context, and its permissions are the context's limited by scope_map.
  • Breaking: DEFAULT_PERMISSION_ACTION_MAP moved from rn_forge.django.auth.drf.mixins to rn_forge.auth.
  • Breaking: depends on rn-forge-auth and imports Principal, Requirement and the authenticator contracts from it. The oidc extra names rn-forge-auth[oidc] instead of rn-forge-web[auth].
  • Breaking: JWKSBearerAuthentication loses its fetch hook, and its cache_timeout now means the key-set lifespan in seconds, default 300 in place of 86400. The new cooldown_duration (default 30 seconds) is the fewest seconds between two key set fetches.
  • The oidc and all extras no longer name rn-forge-commons[auth], which no longer exists.
  • Breaking: AuthorizedAPIView and AuthorizedModelViewSet check PermissionKeyPermission over BaseAPIView and BaseModelViewSet, so UserViewSet, GroupViewSet and PermissionViewSet still require their permission_key. A subclass that relied on the removed mixins' attributes and hooks (credentials, user, is_request_authorized, validate_permissions, validate_object_permissions) must move to a Requirement or a ResourcePolicy. The principal now comes from request.user, the staff and superuser bypass comes from the authorization context, and an action map is the view's permission_action_map.
  • The package declares the MIT licence and is published to PyPI.

Authenticate API clients with the OIDC bearer classes in rn_forge.django.auth.drf.
  • Breaking: the rn_forge.django.auth.basic and rn_forge.django.auth.saml views (BasicLoginAPIView, BasicLoginViewMixin, SAMLLoginAPIView, SAMLLoginViewMixin, SampleSAMLLoginAPIView) are gone, along with the RN_FORGE_DJANGO["AUTH"]["SAML"] setting and AuthSAMLSettings. A SAML IdP federates through a broker that speaks OIDC.
  • Breaking: BaseCredentials and LoginPayload (rn_forge.django.auth.credentials and rn_forge.django.auth.payload), AuthorizationViewMixin and PermissionKeyViewMixin (rn_forge.django.auth.drf.mixins) and AuthorizationPermission (rn_forge.django.auth.drf.permissions) are gone. Check permissions with PermissionKeyPermission and ResourcePolicyViewMixin.
  • Breaking: BaseLoginViewMixin, BaseLoginAPIView and LogoutAPIView (rn_forge.django.auth.drf.authentication) are gone. auth_urlpatterns serves login and logout.
  • Breaking: the saml extra is gone, and with it the python3-saml dependency.
  • Breaking: the RN_FORGE_DJANGO["DRF"]["VIEWS"] settings block (PERMISSION_ACTION_MAP), DRFViewsSettings and DRFViewsSettingsDict are gone; set permission_action_map on the view.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Soft delete in AIP-164's shape. SoftDeleteModelMixin and SoftDeleteQuerySet in rn_forge.django.models add a nullable, indexed delete_time, soft_delete(actor=), undelete(actor=), .live() and .deleted(), with an unfiltered default manager. SoftDeleteMixin in rn_forge.django.drf.views makes DELETE answer 200 with the resource, adds POST {id}:undelete and showDeleted on list, and answers 409 to PUT and PATCH on a deleted resource. WireAutoSchema documents the three.
  • ReadMaskMixin in rn_forge.django.drf: retrieve, list and batch_get accept readMask and answer 200 with only the named fields. BaseModelViewSet includes it, and WireAutoSchema documents the parameter on those actions.
  • BatchGetMixin (GET :batchGet?ids=1&ids=2) and BatchUpdateMixin (POST :batchUpdate, one JSON Merge Patch and optional ifMatch per item) in rn_forge.django.drf.transfer. BatchUpdateMixin has batch_update_requires_if_match, etag_codec and validate_batch_update_item(instance, data). batch_resource_name is shared with BatchCreateMixin.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• BatchDeleteMixin deletes each row through the view's perform_destroy in place of instance.delete(), so a SoftDeleteMixin viewset soft-deletes in a batch. For any other viewset the behavior is unchanged.
  • Breaking: CursorPagination and OrderByFilter use every orderBy term, not the first. ordering_fields may name nullable fields and relation paths, NULL sorts last in both directions, and the orderBy OpenAPI description says it takes a comma-separated list. A view's non-primary-key default ordering supplies the terms when the request gives no orderBy. Page tokens issued before the change are rejected with 400.
  • Breaking: BaseModelViewSet's PATCH now takes application/merge-patch+json (RFC 7396) and answers application/json with 415 and Accept-Patch. PUT and POST still take application/json.
    • The merged document is validated as a full update; a top-level null sets the field to null, and read-only or unknown members are ignored.
    • A versioned instance enforces If-Match on PATCH, and retrieve and PATCH answer with an ETag.
    • New: MergePatchMixin and MergePatchParser, exported from rn_forge.django.drf.
  • Breaking: the import and batch endpoints word their 422 details as rn-forge-web does, which rn-forge-fastapi also uses.
    • A request over transfer.max_rows on :import, :batchCreate and :batchDelete is a 422 problem with detail The import exceeds the limit of N rows. or The batch exceeds the limit of N rows. and no errors member. It was an errors entry with an empty pointer.
    • A :import request with no file part answers This field is required. at /file, not No file was submitted..
    • A missing requests or ids member answers This field is required. at /requests or /ids. An empty list or a non-list still answers A non-empty list is required..
    • validateOnly and prefill accept true or 1, ignoring case, as before; the unsupported and unreadable file details are unchanged in wording.

docs.title: Auth
docs.text:
rn_forge.django.auth binds the login, session, CSRF and authorization design of rn-forge-auth (a separate package, which holds the framework-neutral contracts, login flows and OIDC adapter) to Django and DRF. It serves a browser single-page application through a server-side session, and API clients through bearer tokens, with one account and one authorization model behind both.

The app is installable (label rn_forge_django_auth).

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
An end-to-end configuration with one OIDC provider, local password login and, in development, a fixture-account provider. Install rn-forge-django with the drf, oidc and redis extras.

Settings:

# settings.py
from rn_forge.django.auth import CSRF_MIDDLEWARE, CSRF_SETTINGS, SESSION_SETTINGS

INSTALLED_APPS = [
    "django.contrib.auth",
    "django.contrib.contenttypes",
    "django.contrib.sessions",
    "rest_framework",
    "rn_forge.django.auth",  # run `manage.py migrate` for the link and state tables
    "myapp",
]

MIDDLEWARE = [
    "django.middleware.security.SecurityMiddleware",
    "django.contrib.sessions.middleware.SessionMiddleware",
    # ... your other middleware ...
    CSRF_MIDDLEWARE,
]

globals().update(SESSION_SETTINGS)  # db-backed sessions, the __Host-session cookie
globals().update(CSRF_SETTINGS)  # Angular's XSRF-TOKEN cookie and X-XSRF-TOKEN header

CACHES = {
    "default": {
        "BACKEND": "django.core.cache.backends.redis.RedisCache",
        "LOCATION": "redis://localhost:6379/1",
    }
}

RN_FORGE_DJANGO = {"AUTH": {"PROBLEM_TYPE_BASE": "https://errors.example.com/"}}

REST_FRAMEWORK = {
    "EXCEPTION_HANDLER": "rn_forge.django.drf.exceptions.problem_details_exception_handler",
}

LogoutTokenVerifier.from_issuer reads the provider's discovery document when it is called, so the provider must be reachable at startup.

The Redis cache backend holds login transactions, replay records and revoked session IDs, which every worker must share; the redis extra installs its client. The session cookie is Secure, so serve development over localhost or HTTPS.

The auth objects, built once:

# myapp/auth_config.py
from django.conf import settings
from django.contrib.auth import authenticate
from rn_forge.auth import (
    AuthorizationContextCache,
    DevelopmentAccount,
    DevelopmentIdentityProvider,
    PasswordIdentityProvider,
)
from rn_forge.auth.oidc import BackchannelLogout, LogoutTokenVerifier, OidcProvider
from rn_forge.django.auth import AuthRoutesConfig, CacheReplayStore
from rn_forge.django.auth.accounts import (
    DjangoAccountResolver,
    DjangoAccountStateWriter,
    ProviderPolicy,
)
from rn_forge.django.auth.authorization import DjangoAuthorizationContextProvider
from rn_forge.django.auth.drf import PrincipalSessionAuthentication, sessions_for
from rn_forge.django.auth.drf.oidc import JWKSBearerAuthentication

ISSUER = "https://login.example.com/tenant/v2.0"


def verify_password(username: str, password: str) -> str | None:
    user = authenticate(username=username, password=password)
    return str(user.pk) if user else None


replay = CacheReplayStore()
resolver = DjangoAccountResolver(
    {
        "acme": ProviderPolicy(
            provisioning="jit",
            email_domains=frozenset({"example.com"}),
            authoritative_domains=frozenset({"example.com"}),
        ),
        # A local user is linked once: resolver.link("local", str(user.pk), user)
        "password": ProviderPolicy(),
        "development": ProviderPolicy(provisioning="jit"),
    }
)
contexts = AuthorizationContextCache(
    DjangoAuthorizationContextProvider(), writer=DjangoAccountStateWriter()
)

providers = {
    "acme": OidcProvider(
        id="acme",
        issuer=ISSUER,
        client_id="orders-web",
        client_secret="...",
        redirect_uri="https://app.example.com/auth/callback/acme",
    ),
    "password": PasswordIdentityProvider(verify_password),
}
if settings.DEBUG:
    providers["development"] = DevelopmentIdentityProvider(
        [DevelopmentAccount("alice", name="Alice")], debug=True
    )

config = AuthRoutesConfig(
    providers=providers,
    accounts=resolver,
    contexts=contexts,
    account_state=contexts,  # writes through to DjangoAccountStateWriter
    return_to_prefixes=["/app"],
    default_return_to="/app",
    provider_names={"acme": "Acme SSO", "password": "Password"},
    replay=replay,
    backchannel={
        "acme": BackchannelLogout(
            LogoutTokenVerifier.from_issuer(
                ISSUER, client_id="orders-web", replay_store=replay
            ),
            resolver,
        )
    },
)


class Session(PrincipalSessionAuthentication):
    sessions = sessions_for(config)


class Bearer(JWKSBearerAuthentication):
    jwks_url = "https://login.example.com/tenant/discovery/v2.0/keys"
    issuer = ISSUER
    audience = "api://orders"
    accounts = resolver
    contexts = contexts

A view lists the classes it accepts:

# myapp/api/views.py
from rest_framework.views import APIView

from myapp.auth_config import Bearer, Session


class OrderView(APIView):
    authentication_classes = [Session, Bearer]

The URLconf and the authorization signals:

# myapp/urls.py
from django.urls import include, path
from rn_forge.django.auth import auth_urlpatterns

from myapp.auth_config import config

urlpatterns = [
    *auth_urlpatterns(config, prefix="auth"),
    path("api/", include("myapp.api.urls")),
]

# myapp/apps.py
from django.apps import AppConfig


class MyAppConfig(AppConfig):
    name = "myapp"

    def ready(self) -> None:
        from rn_forge.django.auth.authorization import connect_authorization_signals

        from myapp.auth_config import contexts

        connect_authorization_signals(contexts)

auth_urlpatterns checks the session, CSRF and cache settings when it builds the URLconf and raises ImproperlyConfigured for a configuration it refuses (Defaults and startup checks).

docs.title: Routes and responses
docs.text:
auth_urlpatterns(config, prefix="auth") serves these routes under the prefix. The URL names are rn-forge-auth-<route>. A 401 from any of them is a problem+json response with no WWW-Authenticate header.

Method Path Response GET providers 200, a list of {id, name, kind}. kind is oidc, oauth2, password or development; the development provider is listed only in DEBUG GET login/{provider}?return_to= 302 to the identity provider, with the __Host-login-tx cookie. A return_to outside return_to_prefixes redirects to the error route. An unknown provider is 404 GET login/development?account= In DEBUG only (otherwise 404): without account, an HTML list of the fixture accounts; with it, signs in and redirects to return_to GET callback/{provider} 302 to return_to, or to the error route; 429 when rate limited GET session 200 with the session body, or 401. Always sets the CSRF cookie POST logout 200 {"redirect": url or null}; 401 without a session POST logout/all 200 {"redirect": null}; 401 without a session POST backchannel-logout/{provider} 200; 400 for an invalid logout token; 404 for a provider with no handler POST login/password 200 with the session body, 401 for any failure, or 429

A callback error redirects to error_route (/auth/error) with ?error= set to one of access_denied, account_not_provisioned and login_failed. Details go to the log, never into the URL. A password login failure is one 401 whatever its cause, so the response does not reveal which accounts exist. The login body is JSON or form-encoded {username, password}.

The session body is camelCase: subject (the account ID), provider, roles, permissions, attributes, authTime, amr and expiresAt (the absolute timeout). It omits name, email and picture: the default resolver stores none. Cache-Control: no-store is set on session responses.

The login transaction lives in the cache for 10 minutes behind the __Host-login-tx cookie (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax, Path=/, no Domain). A callback that carries more than one transaction cookie is rejected, and a transaction is consumed atomically, so a callback works once.

docs.title: Sessions and revocation
docs.text:
Sessions are django.contrib.sessions with the db or cached_db engine, in the __Host-session cookie (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax, Path=/, no Domain). The session holds the account ID, the account's session version at login, provider, issuer, external subject, auth_time, amr, session_ref and the ID token (only with rp_initiated_logout), and never permissions: those are computed on each request.

  • Timeouts. A 30-minute sliding idle timeout (idle_timeout) and a 12-hour absolute timeout (absolute_timeout). A normal read moves the idle expiry forward; GET /auth/session reads with touch=False and does not.
  • One read path. Sessions.read deletes the session, and the caller answers 401, when the absolute timeout has passed, the recorded session version differs from the account's, the account is inactive, or the session_ref is revoked.
  • New IDs. Login gives the session a new ID. Call rotate_session(request) after a change to the account's privileges.
  • Logout. /auth/logout ends the current session. /auth/logout/all and a back-channel logout that names only sub bump the account's session version, which ends every session of the account on its next request. A back-channel logout with a sid revokes that session only, until the absolute timeout. With rp_initiated_logout on the provider, /auth/logout returns the identity provider's end-session URL.
  • Disabling. contexts.set_active(account_id, False) (or any change that makes the account inactive) fails the account's next request with 401.

The authorization context cache is local to each process: a change made in another process applies after the cache's ttl (60 seconds by default), or at once through the cache that made it. Lower ttl where that delay matters.

docs.title: CSRF
docs.text:
Every unsafe method on a session-authenticated route is protected by AuthCsrfMiddleware, a CsrfViewMiddleware subclass. The cookie is XSRF-TOKEN and the header X-XSRF-TOKEN, Angular's defaults; the cookie is not HttpOnly so that Angular can copy it into the header.

  • GET /auth/session always sets the cookie, including when it answers 401, so POST /auth/login/password is protected before sign-in. The token rotates at login and at logout.
  • A rejection is the 403 csrf-failed problem (CSRF_FAILURE_VIEW); its reason is logged, never sent. PROBLEM_TYPE_BASE makes it differ in type from a permission denial.
  • Beyond Django's token and origin check, AuthCsrfMiddleware rejects Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site on an unsafe method, even from a trusted origin.
  • Requests with a Bearer Authorization header skip the check, as does the back-channel logout route, which carries a signed token. A Basic header does not: browsers replay cached Basic credentials on their own.
  • CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS lists the other origins that may post. Behind a proxy, Django takes the request's scheme and host from forwarded headers only when SECURE_PROXY_SSL_HEADER and USE_X_FORWARDED_HOST are set, and the forwarded host must be in ALLOWED_HOSTS. Without them a forged X-Forwarded-* header does not make a foreign Origin acceptable.
  • DRF wraps its views in csrf_exempt, so the middleware does not guard them. PrincipalSessionAuthentication calls enforce_csrf(request) for the sessions it authenticates; a custom session class does the same.

docs.title: Accounts and linking
docs.text:
DjangoAccountResolver links external identities to Django users through the ExternalAccount model, unique on (issuer, subject); run the auth app's migration. A ProviderPolicy per provider ID decides what an unlinked identity gets; a provider with no policy is rejected.

  • provisioning="existing" rejects an identity with no account; provisioning="jit" creates one on first login, limited to email_domains when set (which also requires a verified email).
  • authoritative_domains lists the email domains for which the provider is authoritative: only there does a verified email link to an existing user. Unverified emails never link and are not stored on provisioned users.
  • sync(user, identity), passed to the resolver, runs at every login to copy attributes onto the user.
  • resolver.link(issuer, subject, user) links a service account or a local password user explicitly.

A rejected login redirects with ?error=account_not_provisioned, and a login by an inactive account with ?error=access_denied. The session version behind /auth/logout/all is stored by DjangoAccountStateWriter and read by DjangoAuthorizationContextProvider.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
PrincipalSessionAuthentication yields a Principal with mechanism="session" from Sessions.read; request.auth is the SessionInfo. Subclass it and set sessions = sessions_for(config).

PrincipalBearerAuthentication and JWKSBearerAuthentication verify an externally issued token, then resolve its (issuer, subject) through AccountResolver.lookup. They never provision: an unlinked subject, or an inactive account, is 401. The principal's subject is the account ID; its roles and attributes come from the authorization context, and its permissions are the account's, limited to what the token's scopes allow through scope_map:

class Bearer(JWKSBearerAuthentication):
    ...
    scope_map = {"orders:read": frozenset({"orders.list", "orders.read"})}

List the classes on each view or on a shared base view, not in DEFAULT_AUTHENTICATION_CLASSES: that setting is imported while DRF imports its views, and the module that defines these classes imports DRF's views too.

One credential per request. A request with an Authorization header is authenticated by the bearer class alone: an invalid token is 401 even with a valid session cookie, and the session class ignores the request. List the classes a view accepts. A view whose first class is the session class answers an unauthenticated request with 401 and no WWW-Authenticate header; with a bearer class first, it answers with the Bearer challenge. Both need the problem-details exception handler.

docs.title: Bearer tokens in detail
docs.text:
For an API whose callers hold tokens issued by an identity provider (Entra ID, Auth0, Okta, Keycloak), JWKSBearerAuthentication (the oidc extra) verifies the token against the provider's key set. Set jwks_url, issuer, audience, accounts and contexts on a subclass, as in Setup. cache_timeout (300 seconds) is how long a fetched key set is kept, cooldown_duration (30 seconds) the fewest seconds between two fetches, which bounds how often an unknown kid can reach the provider, and algorithms and leeway set the accepted algorithms and the clock skew. Override claims_to_principal() where the provider keeps roles or scopes somewhere non-standard, such as Keycloak's nested realm_access.roles. The authenticator and key set are cached per subclass and process, so define the class once.

Provider jwks_url Entra ID https://login.microsoftonline.com/{tenant}/discovery/v2.0/keys Auth0 https://{domain}/.well-known/jwks.json Okta https://{domain}/oauth2/{authorization-server-id}/v1/keys

To verify tokens some other way, subclass PrincipalBearerAuthentication and set authenticator to any rn_forge.auth.Authenticator, with accounts, contexts and optionally realm. Protect a view with requires(Requirement(all_scopes=...)), a permission class over the principal's scopes and roles, which evaluates identically on rn-forge-fastapi:

from rest_framework.views import APIView
from rn_forge.auth import Requirement
from rn_forge.django.auth.drf import requires


class OrderView(APIView):
    authentication_classes = [Bearer]
    permission_classes = [requires(Requirement(all_scopes=frozenset({"orders:read"})))]

With problem_details_exception_handler installed, missing or invalid credentials are a 401 problem+json with an RFC 6750 WWW-Authenticate: Bearer challenge and a detail that never says why verification failed; valid credentials lacking the scope are a 403 with no challenge.

PrincipalBasicAuthentication is the RFC 7617 twin: it produces a Principal from an authenticator you supply and does not link accounts. It is for local development and simple internal deployments only.

docs.title: Authorization
docs.text:
DjangoAuthorizationContextProvider builds an AuthorizationContext from a user's groups and permissions. Roles are group names. Django app_label.codename permissions become dotted keys: add, change, delete and view of a model map to <app_label>.<model>.create, update, delete and read (view also grants list), so inventory.change_stock is inventory.stock.update. A custom permission keeps <app_label>.<codename>. A staff or superuser account gets the staff or superuser role and every permission key, so the bypass shows in /auth/session; pass catalog= for keys that exist outside Django's permission table. An unknown or inactive user resolves to an inactive context.

Wrap the provider in an AuthorizationContextCache and call connect_authorization_signals(cache) once at startup (Setup): changes to users, groups, permissions and their relations, including those made through the User, Group and Permission viewsets, then invalidate the affected accounts.

On a view, PermissionKeyPermission requires the key built by rn_forge.auth.requirement_for from permission_key and the action, checked against the request's principal; a view without a permission_key requires only an authenticated principal. ResourcePolicyViewMixin applies a ResourcePolicy: scope narrows the queryset, so counts and pages cover only permitted rows, and allows guards each object, answering 404 instead of 403 when policy_hides_existence is true. Both are in rn_forge.django.auth.drf.

from rn_forge.django.auth.drf import PermissionKeyPermission, ResourcePolicyViewMixin


class OrderViewSet(ResourcePolicyViewMixin, ModelViewSet):
    permission_classes = [PermissionKeyPermission]
    permission_key = "orders"
    resource_policy = OrderPolicy()

docs.title: Management viewsets
docs.text: rn_forge.django.auth.drf.views ships ready-to-mount viewsets for the standard Django auth models, wired through AuthorizedModelViewSet: PermissionViewSet, GroupViewSet, UserViewSet. AuthorizedModelViewSet and AuthorizedAPIView set permission_classes = [PermissionKeyPermission], so each viewset requires its permission_key (rn_forge.auth.permission, rn_forge.auth.group, rn_forge.auth.user) combined with the action. Mount them, or rn_forge.django.auth.urls.urlpatterns, which already registers them, under your API root.

docs.title: Rate limits and audit events
docs.text:
POST /auth/login/password and GET /auth/callback/{provider} are rate limited with a fixed-window counter over Django's cache (cache.add and cache.incr), in the cache alias of AuthRoutesConfig.limiter (FixedWindowLimiter). The client is REMOTE_ADDR: Django resolves proxies through its own settings, and X-Forwarded-For is never read here. Password login is limited per client and per submitted username (hashed in the key); callbacks per client only, because no account is known before the response is verified. Each limit is a RateLimit(limit, window), or None for none. A limited request is the 429 too-many-requests problem with Retry-After. Windows are aligned to the clock, so a client can use a limit twice around a window boundary.

Security-relevant events are INFO records on the rn_forge.audit.auth AppLogger channel, in the form audit event=<name> key='value' ...:

Event Emitted when login.success A login starts a session login.failure A login fails (provider, code, reason) logout, logout.all, logout.backchannel A session or sessions end account.provisioned The resolver creates an account (after commit) account.rejected The resolver refuses an identity account.disabled An inactive account logs in, or DjangoAccountStateWriter.set_active(False) runs authorization.denied PermissionKeyPermission or ResourcePolicyViewMixin denies a request rate_limited A request is answered 429

Events carry account IDs, provider IDs, codes and short reasons, and never a token, code, assertion, password, session ID or email address.

docs.text:

docs.title: SAML identity providers
docs.text: rn-forge-django speaks no SAML. A SAML identity provider federates through a broker (Keycloak, Entra ID, Auth0, Okta and others) that runs the SAML exchange and logs the user in to the application over OIDC; configure the broker as an ordinary OidcProvider. The rn-forge-auth login guide, "Connecting a SAML IdP through a broker", has the steps.

docs.title: Base classes
docs.text:
from rn_forge.django.drf.views import (
    BaseAPIView,             # GenericAPIView + request-access + exception context
    BaseModelViewSet,        # ModelViewSet + audit fields + filtering
)

Auth-aware equivalents that additionally enforce PermissionKeyPermission live in rn_forge.django.auth.drf.views (AuthorizedModelViewSet, AuthorizedAPIView) — see Auth.

docs.title: Request access and audit fields
docs.text:
RequestAccessViewMixin (included in BaseAPIView/BaseModelViewSet) exposes get_request_param(), get_request_data(), get_request_value(), get_request_user(), and get_request_auth() so views don't touch RequestUtils directly.

AuditFieldsViewMixin (included in BaseModelViewSet) populates created_by/updated_by from the authenticated user's email ("anonymous" when unauthenticated) on perform_create/ perform_update, and on every item of a batch create.

ModelFilterViewMixin adds default filterset_fields for id, status, and the audit columns, plus an opt-in ?active=true filter for models extending DateRangeModel.

docs.title: Merge patch
docs.text:
BaseModelViewSet includes MergePatchMixin: its PATCH takes application/merge-patch+json (RFC 7396) and answers any other media type with 415 and Accept-Patch. PUT and POST still take application/json. The merged document is validated as a full update. See the API conventions, section 10, in rn-forge-web for the request order and the null rule.

A versioned model (VersionedModelMixin) checks If-Match, and retrieve and PATCH answer with an ETag. Set etag_codec, and merge_patch_requires_if_match = True to make the header required (428 when absent).

from rn_forge.django.drf.views import BaseModelViewSet
from rn_forge.web import EntityVersionETagCodec


class DocumentViewSet(BaseModelViewSet):
    queryset = Document.objects.all()
    serializer_class = DocumentSerializer
    etag_codec = EntityVersionETagCodec()
    merge_patch_requires_if_match = True

PATCH /documents/1
Content-Type: application/merge-patch+json
If-Match: W/"1:1"

{"settings": {"size": null}, "note": null}

A view outside BaseModelViewSet adds MergePatchMixin from rn_forge.django.drf.

docs.title: Partial responses
docs.text:
BaseModelViewSet includes ReadMaskMixin: retrieve, list and batch_get accept readMask and answer 200 with only the fields it names. Fields are selected by their camelCase wire names as the view's serializer declares them: a nested serializer or a list serializer can be reached with a dotted path, any other field (a JSONField included) is a leaf, and a write-only field cannot be selected. A path that names nothing is a 400 problem. See the API conventions, section 20, in rn-forge-web for the rules.

GET /profiles/1?readMask=displayName,address.city

{"displayName": "Ada", "address": {"city": "London"}}

The ETag of a masked read is the resource's. A paginated list masks each of items and keeps nextPageToken. Other actions, and any response that is not 200, ignore the mask. With rn_forge.django.drf.openapi.WireAutoSchema the schema documents readMask on those three actions. A view outside BaseModelViewSet adds ReadMaskMixin from rn_forge.django.drf; read_mask_actions names the actions it applies to.

docs.title: Soft delete
docs.text:
SoftDeleteMixin serves AIP-164 over a model that uses SoftDeleteModelMixin. List it before BaseModelViewSet:

class NoteViewSet(SoftDeleteMixin, BatchDeleteMixin, BaseModelViewSet):
    queryset = Note.objects.all()
    serializer_class = NoteSerializer
    soft_delete_requires_if_match = True  # optional: 428 without If-Match
  • list omits deleted rows unless showDeleted is true or 1; retrieve, batch_get and the other actions see every row.
  • DELETE soft-deletes and answers 200 with the resource and its ETag; a deleted resource is a 404.
  • POST /notes/{id}:undelete restores it. Serve it with CustomMethodRouter; the schema names it notesUndelete.
  • PUT and PATCH on a deleted resource are a 409.
  • BatchDeleteMixin deletes each row through perform_destroy, so the same viewset soft-deletes in a batch; for any other viewset perform_destroy still deletes the row. A deleted id is a 404 for the whole batch.

A versioned instance honours If-Match on DELETE and :undelete. The wire rules are §21 of rn-forge-web's API conventions.

docs.title: Export, import and batch operations
docs.text: Tabular export and import, and batch create and delete, are in rn_forge.django.drf.transfer (the transfer extra) and are not part of the base classes — see Transfer.

docs.title: Serializers
docs.text:
from rn_forge.django.drf.serializers import BaseModelSerializer


class OrderSerializer(BaseModelSerializer):
    class Meta:
        model = Order
        fields = ["id", "reference", *BaseModelSerializer.BASE_MODEL_FIELDS]

BaseModelSerializer renders status through EnumChoiceField ({"code", "name"} shape) and marks the audit columns read-only. NestedReadPrimaryKeyRelatedField writes by primary key but reads through a nested serializer:

from rn_forge.django.drf.serializers.fields import NestedReadPrimaryKeyRelatedField

customer = NestedReadPrimaryKeyRelatedField(
    queryset=Customer.objects.all(),
    serializer_class=CustomerSerializer,
    read_fields=["id", "name"],
)

docs.title: Sorting and paging
docs.text:
OrderByFilter reads AIP-132 orderBy over the view's ordering_fields, and CursorPagination pages in that order. orderBy is a comma-separated list; a field may be nullable or span a relation (author__name), and rows whose value is NULL come last in both directions. The primary key breaks ties.

from rn_forge.django.drf import CursorPagination, OrderByFilter


class PersonViewSet(BaseModelViewSet):
    queryset = Person.objects.all()
    serializer_class = PersonSerializer
    pagination_class = CursorPagination
    filter_backends = [OrderByFilter]
    ordering_fields = ["team", "score", "id"]  # score is nullable

GET /people?orderBy=team,score%20desc&pageSize=2

A page token holds one value per term, so a token issued under another orderBy is a 400.

docs.title: Exceptions
docs.text:
Register the normalized JSON exception handler in DRF settings:

REST_FRAMEWORK = {
    "EXCEPTION_HANDLER": "rn_forge.django.drf.exceptions.drf_exception_handler",
}

ExceptionContextViewMixin (included in the base views) supplies friendlier per-action error messages (e.g. "Error creating records.") consumed by that handler.

docs.title: Fixtures
docs.text:
FixtureManager (requires the fixtures extra) converts Excel workbooks into Django JSON fixtures and can load them with loaddata.

from pathlib import Path

from rn_forge.django.fixtures import (
    ColumnType,
    FixtureColumn,
    FixtureDefinition,
    FixtureManager,
    FixtureManagerConfig,
)

config = FixtureManagerConfig(
    root_path=Path("fixtures"),
    settings_module="myproject.settings",
    fixtures=[
        FixtureDefinition(
            app_label="orders",
            model="product",
            input_file="products.xlsx",
            output_file="products.json",
            columns=[
                FixtureColumn(name="sku"),
                FixtureColumn(name="price", type=ColumnType.DECIMAL),
                FixtureColumn(name="active", type=ColumnType.BOOLEAN),
                FixtureColumn(name="category", type=ColumnType.FOREIGN_KEY),
                FixtureColumn(name="tags", type=ColumnType.MANY_TO_MANY, required=False),
            ],
            key_columns=["sku"],
        ),
    ],
)

FixtureManager(config).prepare_fixtures().load_data()

Each FixtureDefinition reads one worksheet (named after model) from root_path/input/<app_label>/<input_file> and writes Django loaddata-ready JSON to root_path/output/<app_label>/<output_file>.

  • ColumnType.MANY_TO_MANY columns are read from a separate worksheet named after the column, joined back to the main sheet via key_columns.
  • common_fields on a FixtureDefinition are merged into every generated row (e.g. a constant tenant_id).
  • load_data(fixture_models=["orders.product"]) loads a subset; omit it (or pass ["ALL"]) to load everything configured. It bootstraps Django (DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE + django.setup()) if not already configured, using settings_module.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Require the package by version range:

[project]
dependencies = ["rn-forge-django>=0.6,<0.7"]

Extras go in brackets after the name:

dependencies = ["rn-forge-django[drf]>=0.6,<0.7"]

or, from the command line:

uv add "rn-forge-django[all]>=0.6,<0.7"

Base dependencies are Django, rn-forge-commons and rn-forge-web, each required by version range.

Extra Adds drf Django REST Framework integration (views, serializers, exceptions, pagination, idempotency, concurrency, casing) transfer django-import-export + rn-forge-data (tablib, openpyxl), for rn_forge.django.drf.transfer: tabular export and import, batch create and delete openapi djangorestframework + drf-spectacular, for rn_forge.django.drf.openapi oidc djangorestframework + rn-forge-auth[oidc] (pyjwt[crypto]), for rn_forge.django.auth.drf.oidc redis rn-forge-auth[redis], the client for Django's Redis cache backend that holds login transactions and revoked session IDs celery celery, for rn_forge.django.celery fixtures rn-forge-data[pandas], for building Django JSON fixtures from Excel workbooks all Everything above

There is deliberately no messaging extra — rn_forge.django.messaging is Django ORM plus stdlib.

To use the bundled auth app, add "rn_forge.django.auth" to INSTALLED_APPS. For the OpenAPI integration, add "drf_spectacular".

Docs commands:

uv run --directory packages/rn-forge-django --group docs mkdocs serve
uv run --directory packages/rn-forge-django --group docs mkdocs build

docs.title: Messaging: outbox and inbox
docs.text: rn_forge.django.messaging makes publishing an event as reliable as the database change that caused it, and makes handling a redelivered event a no-op.

docs.title: 1. Declare the tables
docs.text:
Add "rn_forge.django.messaging" to INSTALLED_APPS. The models are abstract; your app owns the concrete tables and their migrations:

from rn_forge.django.messaging.models import AbstractInboxMessage, AbstractOutboxMessage


class OutboxMessage(AbstractOutboxMessage):
    pass


class InboxMessage(AbstractInboxMessage):
    pass

docs.title: 2. Write to the outbox in the same transaction as the change
docs.text:
from django.db import transaction


with transaction.atomic():
    order = Order.objects.create(...)
    OutboxMessage.objects.create(
        message_type="order.created",
        destination="orders",
        payload={"orderId": order.pk},
    )

Either both commit or neither does.

docs.title: 3. Relay committed rows to the bus
docs.text:
The bus is any rn_forge.commons.integration.messaging.MessageBus — an Azure Service Bus adapter in production, InMemoryMessageBus in tests. The envelope is yours to define:

from rn_forge.django.celery import RETRYABLE_TASK_KWARGS, make_app
from rn_forge.django.messaging.relay import make_outbox_relay

app = make_app("orders")


def to_envelope(row: OutboxMessage) -> dict:
    return {
        "specversion": "1.0",
        "id": str(row.message_id),
        "type": row.message_type,
        "source": "/orders",
        "time": row.occurred_at.isoformat(),
        "data": row.payload,
    }


relay = make_outbox_relay(
    OutboxMessage,
    bus,
    envelope_builder=to_envelope,
    on_lag_observed=outbox_lag_histogram.record,
)


@app.task(**RETRYABLE_TASK_KWARGS)
def publish_outbox() -> int:
    return relay()

Schedule publish_outbox with Celery beat (or call relay() from a management command loop). Each call publishes at most batch_size rows and returns how many; while relay(): pass drains.

docs.title: 4. Handle inbound events exactly once
docs.text:
from rn_forge.commons.integration.messaging import HandlerRegistry
from rn_forge.django.messaging.consumer import process_event

registry = HandlerRegistry().register("payment.captured", mark_order_paid)


def on_message(event):  # called by your broker consumer
    process_event(event, registry, InboxMessage)

A redelivered event returns False without running the handler. A handler's database writes and the "processed" mark commit together. A failing handler has its error recorded on the inbox row and is re-raised, so the broker can retry or dead-letter it.

docs.title: Guarantees and their limits
docs.text:
• Out: at-least-once. A publish error rolls the whole batch back, so rows already sent in that batch are sent again. Subscribers must dedupe — which is what the inbox is for.
  • Concurrent relays need PostgreSQL. Rows are claimed with select_for_update(skip_locked=True), so two relays take disjoint batches. sqlite has no row locks: run a single relay there. The locking behaviour is tested by the postgres-marked tests, which run when RN_FORGE_DJANGO_TEST_DATABASE_URL points at a PostgreSQL database.
  • No broker adapters here. Azure Service Bus and friends implement the commons MessageBus protocol in their own packages.

docs.title: BaseModel
docs.text:
Nearly all concrete models should inherit from BaseModel (or DateModel/DateRangeModel, which extend it):

from django.db import models

from rn_forge.django.models import BaseModel


class Product(BaseModel):
    sku = models.CharField(max_length=32, unique=True)
    name = models.CharField(max_length=255)

    validate_on_save = True

    def natural_keys(self) -> list[str]:
        return ["sku"]

BaseModel adds:

  • status — an EnumField over the Status enum (Active/Inactive/Error/Deleted/ Expired), defaulting to Active
  • created_by / create_time / updated_by / update_time audit columns (snake_case Python fields and columns)
  • objects = NaturalKeyLookupManager() — enables get_by_natural_key() for fixture loading, driven by natural_keys()
  • TruncateModelMixin.truncate() — TRUNCATE TABLE (or DELETE FROM on SQLite), handy for test teardown
  • opt-in validation-on-save: set validate_on_save = True to have save() call full_clean(); override get_full_clean_exclude() to control which fields are excluded on a partial update_fields save

docs.title: Concurrency and immutability
docs.text:
Two opt-in mixins, listed before the base so BaseModel's validation still runs:

from rn_forge.django.models import BaseModel, ImmutableModelMixin, VersionedModelMixin


class Order(VersionedModelMixin, BaseModel):
    """`version` starts at 1 and is bumped by every save of an existing row."""


class LedgerEntry(ImmutableModelMixin, BaseModel):
    """Any change outside the audit columns, and any delete, raises DomainConflict (409)."""

The version bump survives a partial save(update_fields=[...]). The UPDATE only matches the row at the version the instance was loaded at, so a save from a stale instance — another request saved in between — raises rn_forge.web.VersionConflict (412) rather than silently overwriting it. ImmutableModelMixin re-reads the row on every update — one extra query — and does not guard queryset-level update()/delete().

Turn a stale write into a 412 from a DRF view, and emit the ETag the client sends back:

from rn_forge.django.drf import enforce_version, etag_for


def partial_update(self, request, *args, **kwargs):
    order = self.get_object()
    enforce_version(request, order, required=True)  # If-Match, or a body "version" key
    response = super().partial_update(request, *args, **kwargs)
    order.refresh_from_db()
    response["ETag"] = etag_for(order)
    return response

A mismatch is 412, a missing required precondition 428, an unparseable one 400 — decided by rn_forge.web.check_precondition, not here. The body-version fallback is a Django-only convenience; an API meant to be swappable with a FastAPI one should require the header.

docs.title: Soft delete
docs.text:
SoftDeleteModelMixin adds a nullable, indexed delete_time. List it before BaseModel so that its manager becomes the default one; that manager keeps get_by_natural_key() and adds .live() and .deleted():

from rn_forge.django.models import BaseModel, SoftDeleteModelMixin, VersionedModelMixin


class Note(SoftDeleteModelMixin, VersionedModelMixin, BaseModel):
    text = models.CharField(max_length=255)


note.soft_delete(actor="alice")  # sets delete_time and updated_by, then saves
note.undelete(actor="bob")  # clears delete_time and sets updated_by
Note.objects.live()  # delete_time IS NULL
Note.objects.deleted()  # delete_time IS NOT NULL

The default manager is not filtered, so the admin, related-object lookups and a GET of a deleted resource keep working; the view decides what is visible. A versioned model bumps its version on soft_delete and undelete as on any save. Override get_delete_time() to supply the recorded time. delete_time is independent of status, and Status.Deleted does not mean soft-deleted. The view side is in DRF Views.

docs.title: Generating human-readable codes
docs.text:
from rn_forge.django.models import AbstractSequenceCounter, SequenceGenerator


class SequenceCounter(AbstractSequenceCounter):
    """Your app owns this model and its migration."""


ORDER_CODES = SequenceGenerator("order_code", counter_model=SequenceCounter, prefix="PO-")
ORDER_CODES.generate()  # "PO-000001"
ORDER_CODES.ensure_at_least(5_000)  # after an import: the next code is PO-005001

The counter model is abstract because this package ships no migrations; you declare the concrete model and own its migration. A shape like PO-2026-0001 is a formatter= you pass, not a default.

What is and is not proven. On PostgreSQL a real sequence (nextval) allocates the value; elsewhere the counter row is locked with select_for_update(). The test suite runs on sqlite, which has no row locks, so only the arithmetic is tested — neither the PostgreSQL path nor behaviour under concurrent allocation is covered by this package's suite.

docs.title: Date-based variants
docs.text:
from rn_forge.django.models import DateModel, DateRangeModel


class Holiday(DateModel):
    """Adds a single `date` field."""


class Discount(DateRangeModel):
    """Adds `start_date`/`end_date` plus `is_date_range_active`."""

DateRangeModel.is_date_range_active is True when today falls within [start_date, end_date]; an unset end_date means the range is open-ended.

docs.title: EnumField
docs.text:
from django.db import models

from rn_forge.django.models import BaseEnum, EnumField


class Priority(BaseEnum):
    Low = "L"
    Medium = "M"
    High = "H"


class Task(models.Model):
    priority = EnumField.build(enum_type=Priority, default=Priority.Medium)

EnumField is a CharField that round-trips database values through the enum type. BaseEnum.get_choices() / BaseEnum.lookup(code) return {"code", "name"} dicts, which pairs with EnumChoiceField on the DRF side (see Auth and DRF Views).

docs.title: Other helpers
docs.text:
• ModelUtils.as_dict(instance) / .to_json(instance) — recursively serialize a model instance (including related objects) to JSON-safe primitives.
  • ModelLookupCache — load a reference table once and resolve foreign keys in O(1) instead of per-row queries:
from rn_forge.django.models import ModelLookupCache

cache = ModelLookupCache()
cache.load(Country, "iso_code")
country = cache.get(Country, "AU")

docs.title: OpenAPI and camelCase
docs.text:
An rn-forge-django API and an rn-forge-fastapi API describe themselves the same way: OpenAPI 3.1.0, camelCase property names, the shared ProblemDetail, CheckResult and HealthReport components, and operationIds of the form <resource><Verb>. The wire conventions themselves are specified by rn-forge-web's api-conventions.md; this page is only the Django wiring.

Install the openapi extra (see Installation) and add drf_spectacular to INSTALLED_APPS. Then:

from rn_forge.django.drf.openapi import SPECTACULAR_SETTINGS as RNF_SPECTACULAR

REST_FRAMEWORK = {
    "EXCEPTION_HANDLER": "rn_forge.django.drf.exceptions.problem_details_exception_handler",
    "DEFAULT_RENDERER_CLASSES": ["rn_forge.django.drf.casing.CamelCaseJSONRenderer"],
    "DEFAULT_PARSER_CLASSES": ["rn_forge.django.drf.casing.CamelCaseJSONParser"],
    "DEFAULT_PAGINATION_CLASS": "rn_forge.django.drf.pagination.CursorPagination",
    "DEFAULT_SCHEMA_CLASS": "rn_forge.django.drf.openapi.WireAutoSchema",
}

SPECTACULAR_SETTINGS = {**RNF_SPECTACULAR, "TITLE": "Orders API", "VERSION": "1.0.0"}

That is the whole of it. What each piece does:

Setting Effect CamelCaseJSONRenderer / CamelCaseJSONParser camelCase out; camelCase or snake_case in. Switch off with RN_FORGE_DJANGO["DRF"]["CASING"]["ENABLED"] = False WireAutoSchema operationId = <resource><Verb> (workItemsList, workItemsGet, workItemsCreate, ...), <resource><Action> for an AIP-136 custom method (/orders/<str:pk>:cancel → ordersCancel). Read from rn_forge.web.openapi, which the FastAPI binding reads too. The paginated component keeps drf-spectacular's own name (Paginated<Item>List) — document text is not held identical across stacks SPECTACULAR_SETTINGS pins OAS 3.1.0, always emits ProblemDetail, camelizes component property names, and declares an application/problem+json response for every status the problem handler can render, on every operation importing rn_forge.django.drf.openapi registers bearerAuth / basicAuth security schemes for the principal authentication classes

docs.title: Serving the document, the docs UI, and the API catalog
docs.text:
from rn_forge.django.drf.openapi import openapi_urlpatterns

urlpatterns = [
    *openapi_urlpatterns(),
    # ... your own routes
]

Mounts drf-spectacular's SpectacularAPIView at /openapi.json, SpectacularSwaggerView at /docs, and RFC 9727's /.well-known/api-catalog — an RFC 9264 linkset naming both, plus /readyz. Pass readiness_path= if yours differs.

docs.title: Opaque JSON values
docs.text:
Global casing rewrites every nested key. A field whose value is data keyed by something other than a Python name — a vendor payload, a mapping keyed by SKU — must be declared as RawPassthroughField, which keeps its keys verbatim in both directions:

from rn_forge.django.drf.serializers import RawPassthroughField

class OrderSerializer(serializers.Serializer):
    vendor_payload = RawPassthroughField()

docs.title: The shared components
docs.text: ProblemDetail and HealthReport (and its CheckResult) are the rn_forge.web pydantic models. Name one in @extend_schema(responses=...) and drf-spectacular's pydantic extension emits the component under its shared name, camelCase properties included. The ProblemDetail component is always present. A page is described by the paginator's own get_paginated_response_schema, not by Page.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
from django.db import models

from rn_forge.django.models import BaseModel, EnumField, Status


class Order(BaseModel):
    reference = models.CharField(max_length=64, unique=True)

    def natural_keys(self) -> list[str]:
        return ["reference"]

BaseModel adds status, created_by/create_time/updated_by/update_time, and a NaturalKeyLookupManager default manager — see Models.

Wire a DRF viewset over it:

from rest_framework import serializers

from rn_forge.django.drf.serializers import BaseModelSerializer

docs.title: Wire it to the shared API contract
docs.text:
Errors as RFC 9457 problems, W3C Trace Context on every request, AIP-158 cursor pagination and camelCase JSON — the same wire an rn-forge-fastapi service speaks:

# manage.py, wsgi.py, asgi.py — before Django loads
from rn_forge.django.tracing import instrument  # the `otel` extra

instrument()

from rn_forge.django.security import SECURITY_SETTINGS

MIDDLEWARE = [
    # DjangoInstrumentor (from instrument(), above) inserts its own middleware
    # at position 0 here, ahead of everything below.
    "django.middleware.http.ConditionalGetMiddleware",  # If-None-Match -> 304 on any ETag response
    "django.middleware.security.SecurityMiddleware",  # nosniff, Referrer-Policy, X-Frame-Options, HSTS
    "django.middleware.clickjacking.XFrameOptionsMiddleware",
    "rn_forge.django.security.SecurityHeadersMiddleware",  # Cache-Control, CSP frame-ancestors
    # ... the rest of your middleware
]

globals().update(SECURITY_SETTINGS)  # or assign SECURE_CONTENT_TYPE_NOSNIFF etc. yourself

from rn_forge.django.cors import cors_settings

    "corsheaders",
    # ...
]

    # ... CorsMiddleware goes above CommonMiddleware, if you use one
    "corsheaders.middleware.CorsMiddleware",
    # ...
]

REST_FRAMEWORK = {
    "EXCEPTION_HANDLER": "rn_forge.django.drf.exceptions.problem_details_exception_handler",
    "DEFAULT_PAGINATION_CLASS": "rn_forge.django.drf.pagination.CursorPagination",
    "DEFAULT_RENDERER_CLASSES": ["rn_forge.django.drf.casing.CamelCaseJSONRenderer"],
    "DEFAULT_PARSER_CLASSES": ["rn_forge.django.drf.casing.CamelCaseJSONParser"],

And in the root URLconf:

from rn_forge.django.views import health_urlpatterns

handler404 = "rn_forge.django.exceptions.problem_details_handler404"
handler500 = "rn_forge.django.exceptions.problem_details_handler500"

    *health_urlpatterns(checks={"database": ping_database}, required=["database"]),
]

With the otel extra and instrument(), the request span is the access record: method, path, status and duration.

docs.title: Deprecating a view
docs.text:
from datetime import UTC, datetime

from drf_spectacular.utils import extend_schema
from rn_forge.django.deprecation import deprecated

SUNSET_ANNOUNCED = datetime(2026, 1, 1, tzinfo=UTC)
SUNSET_DATE = datetime(2026, 7, 1, tzinfo=UTC)


class LegacySummaryView(APIView):
    @extend_schema(deprecated=True)  # marks the OpenAPI operation
    @deprecated(deprecated_at=SUNSET_ANNOUNCED, sunset=SUNSET_DATE)
    def get(self, request): ...

@extend_schema(deprecated=True) and @deprecated(...) are both needed: one marks the document, the other stamps the Deprecation/Sunset/Link headers on the wire (RFC 9745, RFC 8594).

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
All configuration lives in a single RN_FORGE_DJANGO dict in your Django settings module:

RN_FORGE_DJANGO = {
    "AUTH": {
        "PROBLEM_TYPE_BASE": "https://errors.example.com/",  # required to mount the /auth routes
    },
    "DRF": {
        "TRANSFER": {
            "MAX_ROWS": 10_000,  # rows per export, import or batch request; None = no cap
        },
        "PAGINATION": {
            "PAGE_SIZE": 50,  # default page size
            "PAGE_SIZE_QUERY_PARAM": "pageSize",
            "MAX_PAGE_SIZE": 200,  # larger requests are clamped, never rejected
        },
        "CASING": {
            "ENABLED": True,  # camelCase renderer/parser; False = plain JSON
        },
    },
}

DRF.PAGINATION is read at request time by CursorPagination and LegacyPageNumberPagination; a page_size or max_page_size set on a pagination subclass wins over it. DRF.CASING switches CamelCaseJSONRenderer and CamelCaseJSONParser — see OpenAPI and camelCase.

Read the resolved, typed settings at runtime via the module-level facade:

from rn_forge.django.settings import rn_forge_django_settings

max_rows = rn_forge_django_settings.drf.transfer.max_rows
problem_type_base = rn_forge_django_settings.auth.problem_type_base

rn_forge_django_settings is a frozen dataclass tree rebuilt automatically whenever Django's setting_changed signal fires for RN_FORGE_DJANGO — this is what makes override_settings(RN_FORGE_DJANGO=...) work transparently in tests. Every field has a default, so an empty or missing RN_FORGE_DJANGO dict is valid.

docs.title: Adding a configurable option
docs.text:
The facade is a frozen dataclass tree — RnforgeDjangoSettings → AuthSettings/DRFSettings → nested settings — built once by _build_settings() in settings.py and rebuilt by the setting_changed handler. A new option needs three edits, in this order:

  1. A field on the relevant *SettingsDict TypedDict, naming the RN_FORGE_DJANGO key (uppercase, as the dict is written).
  2. A field on the matching frozen dataclass, snake_cased, with a default — every field has one, so an absent RN_FORGE_DJANGO stays valid.
  3. Extraction in _build_settings(), using DictUtils.get/_get_mapping for the nested path ("DRF.VIEWS", say).

Skipping step 3 leaves the field permanently at its default, which no test catches unless it asserts the non-default value.

docs.title: Transfer: export, import and batch operations
docs.text:
rn_forge.django.drf.transfer needs the transfer extra (django-import-export and rn-forge-data, which brings tablib and openpyxl). It is not imported by rn_forge.django.drf, so a project that does not use it installs neither. Register viewsets with CustomMethodRouter so the extra actions are served as /orders:import and /orders:batchCreate (AIP-136), not /orders/import.

from import_export import fields, resources, widgets
from rest_framework.viewsets import ModelViewSet

from rn_forge.django.drf.routers import CustomMethodRouter
from rn_forge.django.drf.transfer import (
    BatchCreateMixin, BatchDeleteMixin, ResourceExportMixin, ResourceImportMixin,
)


class OrderExport(resources.ModelResource):
    store = fields.Field(attribute="store__sap", column_name="Store")

    class Meta:
        model = Order
        fields = ("reference", "store", "quantity")


class OrderImport(resources.ModelResource):
    reference = fields.Field(attribute="reference", column_name="REF")
    store = fields.Field(
        attribute="store", column_name="STORE",
        widget=widgets.ForeignKeyWidget(Store, field="sap"),
    )

    class Meta:
        model = Order
        fields = ("reference", "store")
        import_id_fields = ("reference",)
        skip_unchanged = True
        report_skipped = True

    def before_import_row(self, row, **kwargs):
        user = kwargs["user"]  # the request user: set audit fields, authorize the row


class OrderViewSet(
    ResourceExportMixin, ResourceImportMixin, BatchCreateMixin, BatchDeleteMixin, ModelViewSet
):
    queryset = Order.objects.all()
    serializer_class = OrderSerializer
    export_resource_class = OrderExport
    import_resource_class = OrderImport
    export_column_formats = {"Quantity": "#,##0"}


router = CustomMethodRouter(trailing_slash=False)
router.register("orders", OrderViewSet, basename="orders")

A viewset takes only the mixins it needs (BatchGetMixin, BatchCreateMixin, BatchUpdateMixin, BatchDeleteMixin). The wire shapes are those of the transfer section of the rn-forge-web API conventions.

Request Behaviour GET /orders with Accept: text/csv or the XLSX media type, or ?format=csv\|xlsx The JSON list's filters, then Resource.export(); not paginated. Above transfer.max_rows it is a 422 problem naming the cap. Content-Disposition carries filename*. Permission is that of list. POST /orders:import, multipart/form-data file, ?validateOnly=true Upsert through the import resource. 200 {created, updated, skipped, validateOnly}; any row error is a 422 with errors[].pointer = "/rows/<row>/<column>" and nothing persisted. Permission upload. GET /orders:importTemplate, ?prefill=true The import columns, negotiated like an export; prefill adds the filtered rows. POST /orders:batchCreate, {"requests": [...]} Each item through the serializer, all or nothing. 200 {"orders": [...]}. GET /orders:batchGet?ids=1&ids=2 The ids within filter_queryset(get_queryset()), serialized with the view's serializer. 200 {"orders": [...]} in request order. No ids, or more than transfer.max_rows, is a 400; an id outside the filtered queryset is a 404 naming it. POST /orders:batchUpdate, {"requests": [{"id", "patch", "ifMatch"}]} Each patch is a JSON Merge Patch merged into the row and validated through the serializer, all or nothing, in one transaction. 200 {"orders": [...]} in request order. A failed precondition is a 428, 400 or 412 at /requests/<i>/ifMatch; an invalid merge is a 422 at /requests/<i>/patch/<field>. POST /orders:batchDelete, {"ids": [...]} All or nothing, 204. An id outside the filtered queryset is a 404 naming it.

Row numbers in pointers count from 0. A pointer names the column as it appears in the file when the failing field is an import field. An error import-export raises outside field validation (a ForeignKeyWidget that finds no row, or an exception in before_import_row) points at the whole row.

docs.title: Per-item authorization
docs.text:
Override the hooks and return a message to refuse an item; the response is one 403 problem with errors[].pointer naming the item, and nothing is persisted.

  • prepare_batch_create_item(item) runs on each raw item before validation.
  • validate_batch_create_item(item) runs on each validated item, after AuditFieldsViewMixin.prepare_create_data.
  • validate_batch_update_item(instance, data) runs on each row and its validated data, after AuditFieldsViewMixin.prepare_update_data.
  • validate_batch_delete_instance(instance) runs on each instance to delete.

BatchUpdateMixin checks ifMatch for a VersionedModelMixin row, and an unversioned model ignores it. Set batch_update_requires_if_match = True to make a missing ifMatch a 428, and etag_codec to change the validator format, as for MergePatchMixin. BatchGetMixin and BatchUpdateMixin answer under batch_resource_name, which they share with BatchCreateMixin.

In an import resource the same check belongs in before_import_row(row, **kwargs), where kwargs["user"] is the request user; raising there is reported as a row error.

docs.title: Committing the valid rows
docs.text: Set import_rollback_on_validation_errors = False on the viewset to commit the valid rows when the only failures are field validation errors. The response is 200 with the failures under errors. Any other error still rolls the import back.

Django's default model permissions map to <app_label>.<model>.<action>, lowercase: add to create, change to update, delete to delete and view to both read and list. So inventory.change_stock is inventory.stock.update. Any other permission, such as a custom inventory.adjust_stock, keeps its <app_label>.<codename> as the key.

docs.title: PrincipalSessionAuthentication
docs.text:
Bases: BaseAuthentication

Authenticate the login session into a mechanism="session" principal.

Subclass and set sessions, typically to sessions_for(config) of the :class:~rn_forge.django.auth.routes.AuthRoutesConfig given to auth_urlpatterns. request.auth is the session's :class:~rn_forge.auth.SessionInfo. The read extends the idle timeout.

A request with an Authorization header is never authenticated here: list a bearer class first and the header alone decides, so an invalid token is a 401 even with a valid session cookie.

An unsafe method also passes the CSRF check of :func:~rn_forge.django.auth.csrf.enforce_csrf; a failure is the 403 csrf-failed problem.

As the first authentication class of a view, an unauthenticated request is a 401 problem with no WWW-Authenticate header, provided the view uses :func:~rn_forge.django.drf.exceptions.problem_details_exception_handler. A bearer class first keeps the Bearer challenge.

The login session, kept in django.contrib.sessions.

Every read of the session goes through :meth:Sessions.read, which enforces the absolute timeout and the revocation checks. Spread into your settings module: globals().update(SESSION_SETTINGS). The __Host- cookie requires Secure, Path=/ and no Domain. SESSION_SAVE_EVERY_REQUEST must stay false: reading the session then does not extend it.

docs.text:
CSRF protection for the session-authenticated routes.

Django's CsrfViewMiddleware checks the token and, for an Origin or (over HTTPS) Referer header, that the origin is the request's own or in CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS. The request's scheme and host come from forwarded headers only when SECURE_PROXY_SSL_HEADER and USE_X_FORWARDED_HOST say so. :class:AuthCsrfMiddleware also rejects Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site and skips requests that carry a Bearer Authorization header.

Django settings for the CSRF cookie and header.

Spread into your settings module with globals().update(CSRF_SETTINGS), and add :data:CSRF_MIDDLEWARE to MIDDLEWARE. The names are Angular's HttpClient defaults, and the cookie is readable by script, which Angular needs to copy it into the header.

docs.title: Which handler do I want?
docs.text:
Two exception handlers ship, and this package wires neither — name one in REST_FRAMEWORK["EXCEPTION_HANDLER"]:

  • problem_details_exception_handler renders RFC 9457 application/problem+json. It is the wire contract shared with rn-forge-fastapi, so choose it for any new API.   • drf_exception_handler renders this package's original {"path", "error", "message"} body, for existing consumers.

For Django's own routing errors, name rn_forge.django.exceptions.problem_details_handler404 (and problem_details_handler500) in your root URLconf — see Exceptions.

docs.title: rn_forge.django.drf.openapi
docs.text:
OpenAPI through drf-spectacular, held to the same conventions as the FastAPI stack.

Requires the openapi extra. Not re-exported from any facade; import it directly.

Four things an application otherwise gets wrong, each shipped as code:

  • :data:SPECTACULAR_SETTINGS — OpenAPI 3.1.0, camelCase names, the ProblemDetail component always present, and the camelCase and problem-response schema hooks. Spread it into your own SPECTACULAR_SETTINGS and override what you must.
  • :class:WireAutoSchema — the operationId convention, read from :mod:rn_forge.web.openapi so that this stack and the FastAPI one apply one rule rather than two copies of it. A generated client gets the same method names on either — document text otherwise is not held identical across stacks; drf-spectacular's own paginated-component name is kept. Name it as REST_FRAMEWORK["DEFAULT_SCHEMA_CLASS"].
  • :func:problem_responses_hook — declares an application/problem+json response, referencing ProblemDetail, for every status the problem handler can render, on every operation that does not already declare one. The FastAPI binding's FastApiApp.openapi() closes the identical gap on its side.
  • The security-scheme extensions for :class:~rn_forge.django.auth.drf.principal.PrincipalBearerAuthentication and its Basic twin. drf-spectacular discovers extensions by import, so importing this module — which naming :class:WireAutoSchema in settings does — registers them.

The djangorestframework_camel_case postprocessing hook drf-spectacular documents is not used; :func:camelize_schema_hook is its replacement, for the reason given in :mod:rn_forge.django.drf.casing.

Usage::

from rn_forge.django.drf.openapi import SPECTACULAR_SETTINGS as RNF_SPECTACULAR

SPECTACULAR_SETTINGS = {**RNF_SPECTACULAR, "TITLE": "Orders API"}

docs.title: CustomMethodRouter(*args, **kwargs)
docs.text:
Bases: DefaultRouter

A :class:~rest_framework.routers.DefaultRouter with colon-form custom methods.

An @action(detail=False, url_path="batchCreate") is served at /orders:batchCreate and an @action(detail=True, url_path="cancel") at /orders/12:cancel. Custom methods never take a trailing slash. router.register("orders", OrderViewSet, basename="orders")

docs.title: BatchUpdateMixin
docs.text:
Bases: _BatchResourceMixin

Add POST :batchUpdate: {"requests": [{"id", "patch", "ifMatch"}]}, all or nothing.

Each item's patch is an RFC 7396 JSON Merge Patch, merged into the row's current representation and validated through the view's serializer as a full update. ifMatch is the item's precondition, checked when the row is a :class:~rn_forge.django.models.VersionedModelMixin. The response is 200 with the updated resources under the plural resource name, in request order.

A malformed list or item is a 422 problem, an id outside filter_queryset(get_queryset()) a 404, a failed precondition a 428, 400 or 412 pointing at /requests/<i>/ifMatch (a version conflict at save time included), a failed merged document a 422 pointing at /requests/<i>/patch/<field>, and an error string from :meth:validate_batch_update_item a 403 pointing at the item. docs.title: SoftDeleteMixin
docs.text:
Bases: GenericAPIView

Soft delete in AIP-164's shape for a viewset over a soft-deleting model.

The model uses :class:~rn_forge.django.models.SoftDeleteModelMixin. List this mixin before :class:~rn_forge.django.drf.views.base.BaseModelViewSet, which supplies the audit actor and the ETag codec.

  • list and batch_delete omit deleted rows; list includes them when showDeleted is true or 1. Every other action sees all rows.
  • DELETE soft-deletes and answers 200 with the resource and its ETag. A resource that is already deleted is a 404.
  • POST {id}:undelete restores the resource and answers 200 with it.
  • PUT and PATCH on a deleted resource are a 409.

A versioned instance honours If-Match on DELETE and :undelete, after the checks above.
